title: Agent skill finds the cheapest McDonald's China order by combining coupons, cutting ¥47 to ¥21.9
summary: Choosing among dozens of menu items and stacking coupons is hard to do by hand. This agent skill pulls the menu and all coupons via McDonald's China MCP, runs a deterministic optimizer for the cheapest valid combo, and places the order after the user confirms.
agent_role: The agent interprets the request, queries stores, menus, four coupon sources and nutrition data, normalizes it, calls the optimizer, explains the options and creates the order. The user confirms before ordering.
outcome: Author reports a Big Mac meal priced ¥47 drops to ¥21.90 (53% off) in the sample data, and notes that real-account testing showed coupons must be pulled from four sources to find the best combo.
what_they_did: Developer hujjun built a WorkBuddy skill on top of McDonald's China MCP for a McDonald's developer contest. When a user asks for the cheapest way to order something, the agent pulls stores, menu, prices, nutrition data and coupons from four sources. It normalizes the data and hands it to a deterministic Python optimizer that searches for the lowest-priced valid combo. Before the order is created, the price is checked through MCP and the user confirms.
how_it_went: On the sample data, the author reports a Big Mac, medium fries and Coke drops from ¥47.00 to ¥21.90, a 53% saving, using a 1+1 combo coupon. They note that menu prices and coupons in the sample are demo snapshots, so real prices depend on the store.
worth_knowing: In testing with a real account, the author found that querying a single coupon source misses the best combo. Some coupons must be claimed first, and others are store-only. Some store coupons also work only for pickup, not delivery. The arithmetic is left to code because LLMs often get prices and discounts wrong.
prompt: I want to order [items] from [restaurant] near [your location], for [pickup/delivery], with a budget of [amount] and up to [calorie limit]. Use the restaurant's ordering tools to fetch the menu, prices and every available coupon, including ones I can claim but haven't yet. Do the price math in code, not in your head. Respect each coupon's stacking rules and channel limits, and include delivery fees. Show me the top 3 cheapest valid combinations with their totals and the coupons used. Re-check the final price, and wait for my confirmation before you place any order or start payment.

curation.rationale: A clear, reproducible daily-life agent workflow that fetches live menu and coupon data, runs a deterministic optimizer and places orders after confirmation, with code and self-tests; the headline 53% saving is computed on sample snapshot data and it is a contest entry.
